text:
anya: posted a pic of my attic setup — think my router is sitting on a warm beam right under the skylight. internet dips around 2pm when the sun hits the box :sweat_smile: https://imgur.com/abcd123
liam: ouch, heat can totally make radios flaky. which model is it? any error logs?
anya: TP-Link AX3000 (house hand-me-down). logs show interface flaps and a few "phy down" entries around the drop times. no smoke though, so that's a win :grimacing:
jamal: simple first-aid: lift it off the wood (coaster/brick), avoid direct sunlight, and check cabling. heat + cheap plastic = sad wifi.
infra-bot: Automated tip: For consumer APs, heat can trigger thermal throttling and packet loss. Consider relocating to a ventilated surface or using a small fan. If using PoE, verify voltage at the device.
sarah: or zip-tie a tiny USB fan — engineering classics. also run a quick scan for channel overlap: use `iwlist wlan0 scan` on Linux or `airport -s` on mac to see neighbors.
camila: also adorable cat cameo in the pic, 10/10 aesthetic :cat: But for reliability I'd put it on a shelf close to the exterior wall (shaded) and run a short ethernet to avoid distance/attenuation.
anya: thanks all — moving it to a shaded shelf now and swapping the power brick. scheduling a 2pm repro window to see if drops still happen.
liam: if you want a temporary upgrade, I can drop off an Aruba AP for a week to rule out hardware.
anya: that would be amazing, thanks liam :raised_hands:
jamal: if you keep seeing flaps after moving, paste `dmesg | grep -i phy` and we can parse. sometimes a flaky PoE injector looks like thermal issues.
anya: quick update — moved it to a shelf, taped a tiny fan, and zero drops for 90 mins. will monitor overnight and report back.
camila: victory post when it survives a sunny afternoon! :tada:
anya: will do — thanks everyone for the tips and the cat validation :)
